A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GenDA research work in 18 complete, readable pages, including Appendices A–C. Text comparison and page rendering support comparison of all equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original urban-flow reconstruction experiments, including baseline comparisons in Table 1, sensor-strategy results in Table 2, and additional analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original reconstruction experiments and results in Tables 1–2 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The multiscale graph diffusion architecture, sensor conditioning, training objective, and classifier-free guidance procedure in Section 2 and Appendix B are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Bristol urban-flow dataset, six altitude slices, wind directions, and random, cloud, and trajectory sensing scenarios.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain MeshGraphNet, multiscale MeshGraphNet, and LCSVD in Table 1 and the corresponding comparisons. The edited bibliography entry does not change any evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training/test splits, sensor counts, evaluation metrics, training budgets, and sampling settings are unchanged, including the protocols documented in Appendix B.3.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix C retain identical sensor-placement robustness tests, guidance-weight and observation-density analyses, and qualitative reconstruction examples.

E5.justification: Mean and standard-deviation reporting, aggregation across directions and test slices, and descriptions of multiple sensor placements are identical. Run-count and seed disclosures do not change.

E6.justification: All numerical results and graphical findings are identical. For example, Table 1 retains GenDA RRMSE values of 0.310, 0.190, and 0.136 at 300, 3000, and 8000 observations.

T1.justification: The posterior and tempered-guidance formulation, diffusion equations, graph operations, and metric definitions in Section 2 and Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusions retain identical claims about generative assimilation, geometric generalization, reconstruction performance, and sensing flexibility.

C2.justification: Interpretations of guidance, reconstruction errors, and sensor-placement robustness are unchanged, as are the stated scope and future directions concerning temporal dynamics, volumetric reconstruction, and physical constraints.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain identical preprocessing, mesh construction, hyperparameters, hardware, and training/inference details. Data-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The existing Du et al. (2024) reference changes from a ConFiLD preprint entry to a Nature Communications entry with revised authors and title. Its in-text citation and discussion of latent-space turbulent synthesis remain identical; this is a bibliographic metadata update.

P1.justification: The Du et al. reference's author list, title, and publication details are revised, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. All body prose, section ordering, and appendix structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All 11 figures, three tables, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Rendered differences are confined to the reference text and version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: Updating the Du et al. reference to journal metadata is a localized editorial refinement. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, technical documentation, and appendix analyses are identical, so the revision does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
